units.left_text: The LORD called to Moses, and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying,
units.right_text: Then the LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying,

units.left_text: “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘When anyone of you offers an offering to the LORD, you shall offer your offering of the livestock, from the herd and from the flock.
units.right_text: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When any of you brings an offering to the LORD, you may bring as your offering an animal from the herd or the flock.

units.left_text: “‘If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he shall offer a male without defect. He shall offer it at the door of the Tent of Meeting, that he may be accepted before the LORD.
units.right_text: If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he is to present an unblemished male. He must bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting for its acceptance before the LORD.

units.left_text: He shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it shall be accepted for him to make atonement for him.
units.right_text: He is to lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, so it can be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him.

units.left_text: He shall kill the bull before the LORD. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall present the blood and sprinkle the blood around on the altar that is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: And he shall slaughter the young bull before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons the priests are to present the blood and splatter it on all sides of the altar at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

units.left_text: He shall skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
units.right_text: Next, he is to skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.

units.left_text: The sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar, and lay wood in order on the fire;
units.right_text: The sons of Aaron the priest shall put a fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.

units.left_text: and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall lay the pieces, the head, and the fat in order on the wood that is on the fire which is on the altar;
units.right_text: Then Aaron’s sons the priests are to arrange the pieces, including the head and the fat, atop the burning wood on the altar.

units.left_text: but he shall wash its innards and its legs with water. The priest shall burn all of it on the altar, for a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
units.right_text: The entrails and legs must be washed with water, and the priest shall burn all of it on the altar as a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

units.left_text: “‘If his offering is from the flock, from the sheep or from the goats, for a burnt offering, he shall offer a male without defect.
units.right_text: If, however, one’s offering is a burnt offering from the flock — from the sheep or goats — he is to present an unblemished male.

units.left_text: He shall kill it on the north side of the altar before the LORD. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall sprinkle its blood around on the altar.
units.right_text: He shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons the priests are to splatter its blood against the altar on all sides.

units.left_text: He shall cut it into its pieces, with its head and its fat. The priest shall lay them in order on the wood that is on the fire which is on the altar,
units.right_text: He is to cut the animal into pieces, and the priest shall arrange them, including the head and fat, atop the burning wood that is on the altar.

units.left_text: but the innards and the legs he shall wash with water. The priest shall offer the whole, and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
units.right_text: The entrails and legs must be washed with water, and the priest shall present all of it and burn it on the altar; it is a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

units.left_text: “‘If his offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, then he shall offer his offering from turtledoves or of young pigeons.
units.right_text: If, instead, one’s offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he is to present a turtledove or a young pigeon.

units.left_text: The priest shall bring it to the altar, and wring off its head, and burn it on the altar; and its blood shall be drained out on the side of the altar;
units.right_text: Then the priest shall bring it to the altar, twist off its head, and burn it on the altar; its blood should be drained out on the side of the altar.

units.left_text: and he shall take away its crop and its feathers, and cast it beside the altar on the east part, in the place of the ashes.
units.right_text: And he is to remove the crop with its contents and throw it to the east side of the altar, in the place for ashes.

units.left_text: He shall tear it by its wings, but shall not divide it apart. The priest shall burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
units.right_text: He shall tear it open by its wings, without dividing the bird completely. And the priest is to burn it on the altar atop the burning wood. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.[’’]

units.left_text: “‘When anyone offers an offering of a meal offering to the LORD, his offering shall be of fine flour. He shall pour oil on it, and put frankincense on it.
units.right_text: “When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, his offering must consist of fine flour. He is to pour olive oil on it, put frankincense on it,

units.left_text: He shall bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests. He shall take his handful of its fine flour, and of its oil, with all its frankincense, and the priest shall burn its memorial on the altar, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
units.right_text: and bring it to Aaron’s sons the priests. The priest shall take a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the frankincense, and burn this as a memorial portion on the altar, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

units.left_text: That which is left of the meal offering shall be Aaron’s and his sons’. It is a most holy part of the offerings of the LORD made by fire.
units.right_text: The remainder of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the food offerings to the LORD.

units.left_text: “‘When you offer an offering of a meal offering baked in the oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers anointed with oil.
units.right_text: Now if you bring an offering of grain baked in an oven, it must consist of fine flour, either unleavened cakes mixed with oil or unleavened wafers coated with oil.

units.left_text: If your offering is a meal offering made on a griddle, it shall be of unleavened fine flour, mixed with oil.
units.right_text: If your offering is a grain offering prepared on a griddle, it must be unleavened bread made of fine flour mixed with oil.

units.left_text: You shall cut it in pieces, and pour oil on it. It is a meal offering.
units.right_text: Crumble it and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.

units.left_text: If your offering is a meal offering of the pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
units.right_text: If your offering is a grain offering cooked in a pan, it must consist of fine flour with oil.

units.left_text: You shall bring the meal offering that is made of these things to the LORD. It shall be presented to the priest, and he shall bring it to the altar.
units.right_text: When you bring to the LORD the grain offering made in any of these ways, it is to be presented to the priest, and he shall take it to the altar.

units.left_text: The priest shall take from the meal offering its memorial, and shall burn it on the altar, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
units.right_text: The priest is to remove the memorial portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar as a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

units.left_text: That which is left of the meal offering shall be Aaron’s and his sons’. It is a most holy part of the offerings of the LORD made by fire.
units.right_text: But the remainder of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the food offerings to the LORD.

units.left_text: “‘No meal offering which you shall offer to the LORD shall be made with yeast; for you shall burn no yeast, nor any honey, as an offering made by fire to the LORD.
units.right_text: No grain offering that you present to the LORD may be made with leaven, for you are not to burn any leaven or honey as a food offering to the LORD.

units.left_text: As an offering of first fruits you shall offer them to the LORD, but they shall not rise up as a pleasant aroma on the altar.
units.right_text: You may bring them to the LORD as an offering of firstfruits, but they must not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.

units.left_text: Every offering of your meal offering you shall season with salt. You shall not allow the salt of the covenant of your God to be lacking from your meal offering. With all your offerings you shall offer salt.
units.right_text: And you shall season each of your grain offerings with salt. You must not leave the salt of the covenant of your God out of your grain offering; you are to add salt to each of your offerings.

units.left_text: “‘If you offer a meal offering of first fruits to the LORD, you shall offer for the meal offering of your first fruits fresh heads of grain parched with fire and crushed.
units.right_text: If you bring a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, you shall offer crushed heads of new grain roasted on the fire.

units.left_text: You shall put oil on it and lay frankincense on it. It is a meal offering.
units.right_text: And you are to put oil and frankincense on it; it is a grain offering.

units.left_text: The priest shall burn as its memorial part of its crushed grain and part of its oil, along with all its frankincense. It is an offering made by fire to the LORD.
units.right_text: The priest shall then burn the memorial portion of the crushed grain and the oil, together with all its frankincense, as a food offering to the LORD.[’’]

units.left_text: “‘If his offering is a sacrifice of peace offerings, if he offers it from the herd, whether male or female, he shall offer it without defect before the LORD.
units.right_text: “If one’s offering is a peace offering and he offers an animal from the herd, whether male or female, he must present it without blemish before the LORD.

units.left_text: He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and kill it at the door of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall sprinkle the blood around on the altar.
units.right_text: He is to lay his hand on the head of the offering and slaughter it at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Then Aaron’s sons the priests shall splatter the blood on all sides of the altar.

units.left_text: He shall offer of the sacrifice of peace offerings an offering made by fire to the LORD. The fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,
units.right_text: From the peace offering he is to bring a food offering to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails, all the fat that is on them,

units.left_text: and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kidneys, he shall take away.
units.right_text: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.

units.left_text: Aaron’s sons shall burn it on the altar on the burnt offering, which is on the wood that is on the fire: it is an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
units.right_text: Then Aaron’s sons are to burn it on the altar atop the burnt offering that is on the burning wood, as a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

units.left_text: “‘If his offering for a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD is from the flock, either male or female, he shall offer it without defect.
units.right_text: If, however, one’s peace offering to the LORD is from the flock, he must present a male or female without blemish.

units.left_text: If he offers a lamb for his offering, then he shall offer it before the LORD;
units.right_text: If he is presenting a lamb for his offering, he must present it before the LORD.

units.left_text: and he shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and kill it before the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons shall sprinkle its blood around on the altar.
units.right_text: He is to lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it in front of the Tent of Meeting. Then Aaron’s sons shall splatter its blood on all sides of the altar.

units.left_text: He shall offer from the sacrifice of peace offerings an offering made by fire to the LORD; its fat, the entire tail fat, he shall take away close to the backbone; and the fat that covers the entrails, and all the fat that is on the entrails,
units.right_text: And from the peace offering he shall bring a food offering to the LORD consisting of its fat: the entire fat tail cut off close to the backbone, the fat that covers the entrails, all the fat that is on them,

units.left_text: and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kidneys, he shall take away.
units.right_text: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.

units.left_text: The priest shall burn it on the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire to the LORD.
units.right_text: Then the priest is to burn them on the altar as food, a food offering to the LORD.

units.left_text: “‘If his offering is a goat, then he shall offer it before the LORD.
units.right_text: If one’s offering is a goat, he is to present it before the LORD.

units.left_text: He shall lay his hand on its head, and kill it before the Tent of Meeting; and the sons of Aaron shall sprinkle its blood around on the altar.
units.right_text: He must lay his hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the Tent of Meeting. Then Aaron’s sons shall splatter its blood on all sides of the altar.

units.left_text: He shall offer from it as his offering, an offering made by fire to the LORD; the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,
units.right_text: And from his offering he shall present a food offering to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails, all the fat that is on them,

units.left_text: and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kidneys, he shall take away.
units.right_text: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.

units.left_text: The priest shall burn them on the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire, for a pleasant aroma; all the fat is the LORD’s.
units.right_text: Then the priest is to burn the food on the altar as a food offering, a pleasing aroma. All the fat is the LORD’s.

units.left_text: “‘It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings, that you shall eat neither fat nor blood.’”
units.right_text: This is a permanent statute for the generations to come, wherever you live: You must not eat any fat or any blood.”

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.left_text: “Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘If anyone sins unintentionally, in any of the things which the LORD has commanded not to be done, and does any one of them,
units.right_text: “Tell the Israelites to do as follows with one who sins unintentionally against any of the LORD’s commandments and does what is forbidden by them:

units.left_text: if the anointed priest sins so as to bring guilt on the people, then let him offer for his sin which he has sinned a young bull without defect to the LORD for a sin offering.
units.right_text: If the anointed priest sins, bringing guilt on the people, he must bring to the LORD a young bull without blemish as a sin offering for the sin he has committed.

units.left_text: He shall bring the bull to the door of the Tent of Meeting before the LORD; and he shall lay his hand on the head of the bull, and kill the bull before the LORD.
units.right_text: He must bring the bull to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting before the LORD, lay his hand on the bull’s head, and slaughter it before the LORD.

units.left_text: The anointed priest shall take some of the blood of the bull, and bring it to the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: Then the anointed priest shall take some of the bull’s blood and bring it into the Tent of Meeting.

units.left_text: The priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before the LORD, before the veil of the sanctuary.
units.right_text: The priest is to dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of it seven times before the LORD, in front of the veil of the sanctuary.

units.left_text: The priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of sweet incense before the LORD, which is in the Tent of Meeting; and he shall pour out the rest of the blood of the bull at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: The priest must then put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that is before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting. And he is to pour out the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

units.left_text: He shall take all the fat of the bull of the sin offering from it: the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,
units.right_text: Then he shall remove all the fat from the bull of the sin offering— the fat that covers the entrails, all the fat that is on them,

units.left_text: and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kidneys, he shall remove,
units.right_text: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys—

units.left_text: as it is removed from the bull of the sacrifice of peace offerings. The priest shall burn them on the altar of burnt offering.
units.right_text: just as the fat is removed from the ox of the peace offering. Then the priest shall burn them on the altar of burnt offering.

units.left_text: He shall carry the bull’s skin, all its meat, with its head, and with its legs, its innards, and its dung
units.right_text: But the hide of the bull and all its flesh, with its head and legs and its entrails and dung—

units.left_text: —all the rest of the bull—outside of the camp to a clean place where the ashes are poured out, and burn it on wood with fire. It shall be burned where the ashes are poured out.
units.right_text: all the rest of the bull— he must take outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place where the ashes are poured out, and there he must burn it on a wood fire on the ash heap.

units.left_text: “‘If the whole congregation of Israel sins, and the thing is hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they have done any of the things which the LORD has commanded not to be done, and are guilty;
units.right_text: Now if the whole congregation of Israel strays unintentionally and the matter escapes the notice of the assembly so that they violate any of the LORD’s commandments and incur guilt by doing what is forbidden,

units.left_text: when the sin in which they have sinned is known, then the assembly shall offer a young bull for a sin offering, and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: when they become aware of the sin they have committed, then the assembly must bring a young bull as a sin offering and present it before the Tent of Meeting.

units.left_text: The elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the head of the bull before the LORD; and the bull shall be killed before the LORD.
units.right_text: The elders of the congregation are to lay their hands on the bull’s head before the LORD, and it shall be slaughtered before the LORD.

units.left_text: The anointed priest shall bring some of the blood of the bull to the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: Then the anointed priest is to bring some of the bull’s blood into the Tent of Meeting,

units.left_text: The priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD, before the veil.
units.right_text: and he is to dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD in front of the veil.

units.left_text: He shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar which is before the LORD, that is in the Tent of Meeting; and the rest of the blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: He is also to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that is before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting, and he must pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

units.left_text: All its fat he shall take from it, and burn it on the altar.
units.right_text: And he is to remove all the fat from it and burn it on the altar.

units.left_text: He shall do this with the bull; as he did with the bull of the sin offering, so he shall do with this; and the priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven.
units.right_text: He shall offer this bull just as he did the bull for the sin offering; in this way the priest will make atonement on their behalf, and they will be forgiven.

units.left_text: He shall carry the bull outside the camp, and burn it as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering for the assembly.
units.right_text: Then he is to take the bull outside the camp and burn it, just as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering for the assembly.

units.left_text: “‘When a ruler sins, and unwittingly does any one of all the things which the LORD his God has commanded not to be done, and is guilty,
units.right_text: When a leader sins unintentionally and does what is prohibited by any of the commandments of the LORD his God, he incurs guilt.

units.left_text: if his sin in which he has sinned is made known to him, he shall bring as his offering a goat, a male without defect.
units.right_text: When he becomes aware of the sin he has committed, he must bring an unblemished male goat as his offering.

units.left_text: He shall lay his hand on the head of the goat, and kill it in the place where they kill the burnt offering before the LORD. It is a sin offering.
units.right_text: He is to lay his hand on the head of the goat and slaughter it at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD. It is a sin offering.

units.left_text: The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He shall pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.
units.right_text: Then the priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

units.left_text: All its fat he shall burn on the altar, like the fat of the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin, and he will be forgiven.
units.right_text: He must burn all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the peace offerings; thus the priest will make atonement for that man’s sin, and he will be forgiven.

units.left_text: “‘If anyone of the common people sins unwittingly, in doing any of the things which the LORD has commanded not to be done, and is guilty,
units.right_text: And if one of the common people sins unintentionally and does what is prohibited by any of the LORD’s commandments, he incurs guilt.

units.left_text: if his sin which he has sinned is made known to him, then he shall bring for his offering a goat, a female without defect, for his sin which he has sinned.
units.right_text: When he becomes aware of the sin he has committed, he must bring an unblemished female goat as his offering for that sin.

units.left_text: He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and kill the sin offering in the place of burnt offering.
units.right_text: He is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it at the place of the burnt offering.

units.left_text: The priest shall take some of its blood with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering; and the rest of its blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar.
units.right_text: Then the priest is to take some of its blood with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

units.left_text: All its fat he shall take away, like the fat is taken away from the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall burn it on the altar for a pleasant aroma to the LORD; and the priest shall make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.
units.right_text: Then he is to remove all the fat, just as it is removed from the peace offering, and the priest is to burn it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. In this way the priest will make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.

units.left_text: “‘If he brings a lamb as his offering for a sin offering, he shall bring a female without defect.
units.right_text: If, however, he brings a lamb as a sin offering, he must bring an unblemished female.

units.left_text: He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and kill it for a sin offering in the place where they kill the burnt offering.
units.right_text: And he is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it as a sin offering at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.

units.left_text: The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering; and all the rest of its blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar.
units.right_text: Then the priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.

units.left_text: He shall remove all its fat, like the fat of the lamb is removed from the sacrifice of peace offerings. The priest shall burn them on the altar, on the offerings of the LORD made by fire. The priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin that he has sinned, and he will be forgiven.
units.right_text: And he shall remove all the fat, just as the fat of the lamb is removed from the peace offerings, and he shall burn it on the altar along with the food offerings to the LORD. In this way the priest will make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.[’’]

units.left_text: “‘If anyone sins, in that he hears a public adjuration to testify, he being a witness, whether he has seen or known, if he doesn’t report it, then he shall bear his iniquity.
units.right_text: “If someone sins by failing to testify when he hears a public charge about something he has witnessed, whether he has seen it or learned of it, he shall bear the iniquity.

units.left_text: “‘Or if anyone touches any unclean thing, whether it is the carcass of an unclean animal, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of unclean creeping things, and it is hidden from him, and he is unclean, then he shall be guilty.
units.right_text: Or if a person touches anything unclean— whether the carcass of any unclean wild animal or livestock or crawling creature— even if he is unaware of it, he is unclean and guilty.

units.left_text: “‘Or if he touches the uncleanness of man, whatever his uncleanness is with which he is unclean, and it is hidden from him; when he knows of it, then he shall be guilty.
units.right_text: Or if he touches human uncleanness— anything by which one becomes unclean— even if he is unaware of it, when he realizes it, he is guilty.

units.left_text: “‘Or if anyone swears rashly with his lips to do evil or to do good—whatever it is that a man might utter rashly with an oath, and it is hidden from him—when he knows of it, then he will be guilty of one of these.
units.right_text: Or if someone swears thoughtlessly with his lips to do anything good or evil— in whatever matter a man may rashly pronounce an oath— even if he is unaware of it, when he realizes it, he is guilty in the matter.

units.left_text: It shall be, when he is guilty of one of these, he shall confess that in which he has sinned;
units.right_text: If someone incurs guilt in one of these ways, he must confess the sin he has committed,

units.left_text: and he shall bring his trespass offering to the LORD for his sin which he has sinned: a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, for a sin offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin.
units.right_text: and he must bring his guilt offering to the LORD for the sin he has committed: a female lamb or goat from the flock as a sin offering. And the priest will make atonement for him concerning his sin.

units.left_text: “‘If he can’t afford a lamb, then he shall bring his trespass offering for that in which he has sinned, two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, to the LORD; one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering.
units.right_text: If, however, he cannot afford a lamb, he may bring to the LORD as restitution for his sin two turtledoves or two young pigeons — one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering.

units.left_text: He shall bring them to the priest, who shall first offer the one which is for the sin offering. He shall wring off its head from its neck, but shall not sever it completely.
units.right_text: He is to bring them to the priest, who shall first present the one for the sin offering. He is to twist its head at the front of its neck without severing it;

units.left_text: He shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar; and the rest of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
units.right_text: then he is to sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, while the rest of the blood is drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.

units.left_text: He shall offer the second for a burnt offering, according to the ordinance; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin which he has sinned, and he shall be forgiven.
units.right_text: And the priest must prepare the second bird as a burnt offering according to the ordinance. In this way the priest will make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.

units.left_text: “‘But if he can’t afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, then he shall bring as his offering for that in which he has sinned, one tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering. He shall put no oil on it, and he shall not put any frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.
units.right_text: But if he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he may bring a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He must not put olive oil or frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.

units.left_text: He shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take his handful of it as the memorial portion, and burn it on the altar, on the offerings of the LORD made by fire. It is a sin offering.
units.right_text: He is to bring it to the priest, who shall take a handful from it as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar atop the food offerings to the LORD; it is a sin offering.

units.left_text: The priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin that he has sinned in any of these things, and he will be forgiven; and the rest shall be the priest’s, as the meal offering.’”
units.right_text: In this way the priest will make atonement for him for any of these sins he has committed, and he will be forgiven. The remainder will belong to the priest, like the grain offering.”

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.left_text: “If anyone commits a trespass, and sins unwittingly regarding the LORD’s holy things, then he shall bring his trespass offering to the LORD: a ram without defect from the flock, according to your estimation in silver by shekels, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, for a trespass offering.
units.right_text: “If someone acts unfaithfully and sins unintentionally against any of the LORD’s holy things, he must bring his guilt offering to the LORD: an unblemished ram from the flock, of proper value in silver shekels according to the sanctuary shekel; it is a guilt offering.

units.left_text: He shall make restitution for that which he has done wrong regarding the holy thing, and shall add a fifth part to it, and give it to the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the trespass offering, and he will be forgiven.
units.right_text: Regarding any holy thing he has harmed, he must make restitution by adding a fifth of its value to it and giving it to the priest, who will make atonement on his behalf with the ram as a guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.

units.left_text: “If anyone sins, doing any of the things which the LORD has commanded not to be done, though he didn’t know it, he is still guilty, and shall bear his iniquity.
units.right_text: If someone sins and violates any of the LORD’s commandments even though he was unaware, he is guilty and shall bear his punishment.

units.left_text: He shall bring a ram without defect from of the flock, according to your estimation, for a trespass offering, to the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning the thing in which he sinned and didn’t know it, and he will be forgiven.
units.right_text: He is to bring to the priest an unblemished ram of proper value from the flock as a guilt offering. Then the priest will make atonement on his behalf for the wrong he has committed in ignorance, and he will be forgiven.

units.left_text: It is a trespass offering. He is certainly guilty before the LORD.”
units.right_text: It is a guilt offering; he was certainly guilty before the LORD.”

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.right_text: And the LORD said to Moses,

units.left_text: “If anyone sins, and commits a trespass against the LORD, and deals falsely with his neighbor in a matter of deposit, or of bargain, or of robbery, or has oppressed his neighbor,
units.right_text: “If someone sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor in regard to a deposit or security entrusted to him or stolen, or if he extorts his neighbor

units.left_text: or has found that which was lost, and lied about it, and swearing to a lie—in any of these things that a man sins in his actions—
units.right_text: or finds lost property and lies about it and swears falsely, or if he commits any such sin that a man might commit—

units.left_text: then it shall be, if he has sinned, and is guilty, he shall restore that which he took by robbery, or the thing which he has gotten by oppression, or the deposit which was committed to him, or the lost thing which he found,
units.right_text: once he has sinned and becomes guilty, he must return what he has stolen or taken by extortion, or the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost property he found,

units.left_text: or any thing about which he has sworn falsely: he shall restore it in full, and shall add a fifth part more to it. He shall return it to him to whom it belongs in the day of his being found guilty.
units.right_text: or anything else about which he has sworn falsely.

units.left_text: He shall bring his trespass offering to the LORD: a ram without defect from the flock, according to your estimation, for a trespass offering, to the priest.
units.right_text: Then he must bring to the priest his guilt offering to the LORD: an unblemished ram of proper value from the flock.

units.left_text: The priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven concerning whatever he does to become guilty.”
units.right_text: In this way the priest will make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for anything he may have done to incur guilt.”

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.left_text: “Command Aaron and his sons, saying, ‘This is the law of the burnt offering: the burnt offering shall be on the hearth on the altar all night until the morning; and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it.
units.right_text: “Command Aaron and his sons that this is the law of the burnt offering: The burnt offering is to remain on the hearth of the altar all night, until morning, and the fire must be kept burning on the altar.

units.left_text: The priest shall put on his linen garment, and he shall put on his linen trousers upon his body; and he shall remove the ashes from where the fire has consumed the burnt offering on the altar, and he shall put them beside the altar.
units.right_text: And the priest shall put on his linen robe and linen undergarments, and he shall remove from the altar the ashes of the burnt offering that the fire has consumed and place them beside it.

units.left_text: He shall take off his garments, and put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
units.right_text: Then he must take off his garments, put on other clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place.

units.left_text: The fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it, it shall not go out; and the priest shall burn wood on it every morning. He shall lay the burnt offering in order upon it, and shall burn on it the fat of the peace offerings.
units.right_text: The fire on the altar shall be kept burning; it must not be extinguished. Every morning the priest is to add wood to the fire, arrange the burnt offering on it, and burn the fat portions of the peace offerings on it.

units.left_text: Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out.
units.right_text: The fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it must not be extinguished.

units.left_text: “‘This is the law of the meal offering: the sons of Aaron shall offer it before the LORD, before the altar.
units.right_text: Now this is the law of the grain offering: Aaron’s sons shall present it before the LORD in front of the altar.

units.left_text: He shall take from there his handful of the fine flour of the meal offering, and of its oil, and all the frankincense which is on the meal offering, and shall burn it on the altar for a pleasant aroma, as its memorial portion, to the LORD.
units.right_text: The priest is to remove a handful of fine flour and olive oil, together with all the frankincense from the grain offering, and burn the memorial portion on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

units.left_text: That which is left of it Aaron and his sons shall eat. It shall be eaten without yeast in a holy place. They shall eat it in the court of the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: Aaron and his sons are to eat the remainder. It must be eaten without leaven in a holy place; they are to eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.

units.left_text: It shall not be baked with yeast. I have given it as their portion of my offerings made by fire. It is most holy, as are the sin offering and the trespass offering.
units.right_text: It must not be baked with leaven; I have assigned it as their portion of My food offerings. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.

units.left_text: Every male among the children of Aaron shall eat of it, as their portion forever throughout your generations, from the offerings of the LORD made by fire. Whoever touches them shall be holy.’”
units.right_text: Any male among the sons of Aaron may eat it. This is a permanent portion from the food offerings to the LORD for the generations to come. Anything that touches them will become holy.”

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.left_text: “This is the offering of Aaron and of his sons, which they shall offer to the LORD in the day when he is anointed: one tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering perpetually, half of it in the morning, and half of it in the evening.
units.right_text: “This is the offering that Aaron and his sons must present to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half in the evening.

units.left_text: It shall be made with oil in a griddle. When it is soaked, you shall bring it in. You shall offer the meal offering in baked pieces for a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
units.right_text: It shall be prepared with oil on a griddle; you are to bring it well-kneaded and present it as a grain offering broken in pieces, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

units.left_text: The anointed priest that will be in his place from among his sons shall offer it. By a statute forever, it shall be wholly burned to the LORD.
units.right_text: The priest, who is one of Aaron’s sons and will be anointed to take his place, is to prepare it. As a permanent portion for the LORD, it must be burned completely.

units.left_text: Every meal offering of a priest shall be wholly burned. It shall not be eaten.”
units.right_text: Every grain offering for a priest shall be burned completely; it is not to be eaten.”

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.right_text: And the LORD said to Moses,

units.left_text: “Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, ‘This is the law of the sin offering: in the place where the burnt offering is killed, the sin offering shall be killed before the LORD. It is most holy.
units.right_text: “Tell Aaron and his sons that this is the law of the sin offering: In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering shall be slaughtered before the LORD; it is most holy.

units.left_text: The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: The priest who offers it shall eat it; it must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.

units.left_text: Whatever shall touch its flesh shall be holy. When there is any of its blood sprinkled on a garment, you shall wash that on which it was sprinkled in a holy place.
units.right_text: Anything that touches its flesh will become holy, and if any of the blood is spattered on a garment, you must wash it in a holy place.

units.left_text: But the earthen vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken; and if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, it shall be scoured, and rinsed in water.
units.right_text: The clay pot in which the sin offering is boiled must be broken; if it is boiled in a bronze pot, the pot must be scoured and rinsed with water.

units.left_text: Every male among the priests shall eat of it. It is most holy.
units.right_text: Any male among the priests may eat it; it is most holy.

units.left_text: No sin offering, of which any of the blood is brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place, shall be eaten. It shall be burned with fire.
units.right_text: But no sin offering may be eaten if its blood has been brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place; it must be burned.[’’]

units.left_text: “‘This is the law of the trespass offering: It is most holy.
units.right_text: “Now this is the law of the guilt offering, which is most holy:

units.left_text: In the place where they kill the burnt offering, he shall kill the trespass offering; and its blood he shall sprinkle around on the altar.
units.right_text: The guilt offering must be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and the priest shall splatter its blood on all sides of the altar.

units.left_text: He shall offer all of its fat: the fat tail, and the fat that covers the innards,
units.right_text: And all the fat from it shall be offered: the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails,

units.left_text: and he shall take away the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kidneys;
units.right_text: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which is to be removed with the kidneys.

units.left_text: and the priest shall burn them on the altar for an offering made by fire to the LORD: it is a trespass offering.
units.right_text: The priest shall burn them on the altar as a food offering to the LORD; it is a guilt offering.

units.left_text: Every male among the priests may eat of it. It shall be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.
units.right_text: Every male among the priests may eat of it. It must be eaten in a holy place; it is most holy.

units.left_text: “‘As is the sin offering, so is the trespass offering; there is one law for them. The priest who makes atonement with them shall have it.
units.right_text: The guilt offering is like the sin offering; the same law applies to both. It belongs to the priest who makes atonement with it.

units.left_text: The priest who offers any man’s burnt offering shall have for himself the skin of the burnt offering which he has offered.
units.right_text: As for the priest who presents a burnt offering for anyone, the hide of that offering belongs to him.

units.left_text: Every meal offering that is baked in the oven, and all that is prepared in the pan and on the griddle, shall be the priest’s who offers it.
units.right_text: Likewise , every grain offering that is baked in an oven or cooked in a pan or on a griddle belongs to the priest who presents it,

units.left_text: Every meal offering, mixed with oil or dry, belongs to all the sons of Aaron, one as well as another.
units.right_text: and every grain offering, whether dry or mixed with oil, belongs equally to all the sons of Aaron.

units.left_text: “‘This is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings, which one shall offer to the LORD:
units.right_text: Now this is the law of the peace offering that one may present to the LORD:

units.left_text: If he offers it for a thanksgiving, then he shall offer with the sacrifice of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and cakes mixed with oil.
units.right_text: If he offers it in thanksgiving, then along with the sacrifice of thanksgiving he shall offer unleavened cakes mixed with olive oil, unleavened wafers coated with oil, and well-kneaded cakes of fine flour mixed with oil.

units.left_text: He shall offer his offering with the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving with cakes of leavened bread.
units.right_text: Along with his peace offering of thanksgiving he is to present an offering with cakes of leavened bread.

units.left_text: Of it he shall offer one out of each offering for a heave offering to the LORD. It shall be the priest’s who sprinkles the blood of the peace offerings.
units.right_text: From the cakes he must present one portion of each offering as a contribution to the LORD. It belongs to the priest who sprinkles the blood of the peace offering.

units.left_text: The flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten on the day of his offering. He shall not leave any of it until the morning.
units.right_text: The meat of the sacrifice of his peace offering of thanksgiving must be eaten on the day he offers it; none of it may be left until morning.

units.left_text: “‘But if the sacrifice of his offering is a vow, or a free will offering, it shall be eaten on the day that he offers his sacrifice. On the next day what remains of it shall be eaten,
units.right_text: If, however, the sacrifice he offers is a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day he presents his sacrifice, but the remainder may be eaten on the next day.

units.left_text: but what remains of the meat of the sacrifice on the third day shall be burned with fire.
units.right_text: But any meat of the sacrifice remaining until the third day must be burned up.

units.left_text: If any of the meat of the sacrifice of his peace offerings is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted, and it shall not be credited to him who offers it. It will be an abomination, and the soul who eats any of it will bear his iniquity.
units.right_text: If any of the meat from his peace offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not be credited to the one who presented it; it shall be an abomination, and the one who eats of it shall bear his iniquity.

units.left_text: “‘The meat that touches any unclean thing shall not be eaten. It shall be burned with fire. As for the meat, everyone who is clean may eat it;
units.right_text: Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten; it is to be burned up. As for any other meat, anyone who is ceremonially clean may eat it.

units.left_text: but the soul who eats of the meat of the sacrifice of peace offerings that belongs to the LORD, having his uncleanness on him, that soul shall be cut off from his people.
units.right_text: But if anyone who is unclean eats meat from the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.

units.left_text: When anyone touches any unclean thing, the uncleanness of man, or an unclean animal, or any unclean abomination, and eats some of the meat of the sacrifice of peace offerings which belong to the LORD, that soul shall be cut off from his people.’”
units.right_text: If one touches anything unclean, whether human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean, detestable thing, and then eats any of the meat of the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.”

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.left_text: “Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘You shall eat no fat, of bull, or sheep, or goat.
units.right_text: “Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘You are not to eat any of the fat of an ox, a sheep, or a goat.

units.left_text: The fat of that which dies of itself, and the fat of that which is torn of animals, may be used for any other service, but you shall in no way eat of it.
units.right_text: The fat of an animal found dead or mauled by wild beasts may be used for any other purpose, but you must not eat it.

units.left_text: For whoever eats the fat of the animal which men offer as an offering made by fire to the LORD, even the soul who eats it shall be cut off from his people.
units.right_text: If anyone eats the fat of an animal from which a food offering may be presented to the LORD, the one who eats it must be cut off from his people.

units.left_text: You shall not eat any blood, whether it is of bird or of animal, in any of your dwellings.
units.right_text: You must not eat the blood of any bird or animal in any of your dwellings.

units.left_text: Whoever it is who eats any blood, that soul shall be cut off from his people.’”
units.right_text: If anyone eats blood, that person must be cut off from his people.’”

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.left_text: “Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘He who offers the sacrifice of his peace offerings to the LORD shall bring his offering to the LORD out of the sacrifice of his peace offerings.
units.right_text: “Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘Anyone who presents a peace offering to the LORD must bring it as his sacrifice to the LORD.

units.left_text: With his own hands he shall bring the offerings of the LORD made by fire. He shall bring the fat with the breast, that the breast may be waved for a wave offering before the LORD.
units.right_text: With his own hands he is to bring the food offerings to the LORD; he shall bring the fat, together with the breast, and wave the breast as a wave offering before the LORD.

units.left_text: The priest shall burn the fat on the altar, but the breast shall be Aaron’s and his sons’.
units.right_text: The priest is to burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.

units.left_text: The right thigh you shall give to the priest for a heave offering out of the sacrifices of your peace offerings.
units.right_text: And you are to give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your peace offering.

units.left_text: He among the sons of Aaron who offers the blood of the peace offerings, and the fat, shall have the right thigh for a portion.
units.right_text: The son of Aaron who presents the blood and fat of the peace offering shall have the right thigh as a portion.

units.left_text: For the waved breast and the heaved thigh I have taken from the children of Israel out of the sacrifices of their peace offerings, and have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as their portion forever from the children of Israel.’”
units.right_text: I have taken from the sons of Israel the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution of their peace offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a permanent portion from the sons of Israel.’”

units.left_text: This is the consecrated portion of Aaron, and the consecrated portion of his sons, out of the offerings of the LORD made by fire, in the day when he presented them to minister to the LORD in the priest’s office;
units.right_text: This is the portion of the food offerings to the LORD for Aaron and his sons since the day they were presented to serve the LORD as priests.

units.left_text: which the LORD commanded to be given them of the children of Israel, in the day that he anointed them. It is their portion forever throughout their generations.
units.right_text: On the day they were anointed, the LORD commanded that this be given them by the sons of Israel. It is a permanent portion for the generations to come.

units.left_text: This is the law of the burnt offering, the meal offering, the sin offering, the trespass offering, the consecration, and the sacrifice of peace offerings
units.right_text: This is the law of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the peace offering,

units.left_text: which the LORD commanded Moses in Mount Sinai in the day that he commanded the children of Israel to offer their offerings to the LORD, in the wilderness of Sinai.
units.right_text: which the LORD gave Moses on Mount Sinai on the day He commanded the Israelites to present their offerings to the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai.

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.left_text: “Take Aaron and his sons with him, and the garments, and the anointing oil, and the bull of the sin offering, and the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread;
units.right_text: “Take Aaron and his sons, their garments, the anointing oil, the bull of the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread,

units.left_text: and assemble all the congregation at the door of the Tent of Meeting.”
units.right_text: and assemble the whole congregation at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.”

units.left_text: Moses did as the LORD commanded him; and the congregation was assembled at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: So Moses did as the LORD had commanded him, and the assembly gathered at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

units.left_text: Moses said to the congregation, “This is the thing which the LORD has commanded to be done.”
units.right_text: And Moses said to them, “This is what the LORD has commanded to be done.”

units.left_text: Moses brought Aaron and his sons, and washed them with water.
units.right_text: Then Moses presented Aaron and his sons and washed them with water.

units.left_text: He put the tunic on him, tied the sash on him, clothed him with the robe, put the ephod on him, and he tied the skillfully woven band of the ephod on him and fastened it to him with it.
units.right_text: He put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around him, clothed him with the robe, and put the ephod on him. He tied the woven band of the ephod around him and fastened it to him.

units.left_text: He placed the breastplate on him. He put the Urim and Thummim in the breastplate.
units.right_text: Then he put the breastpiece on him and placed the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece.

units.left_text: He set the turban on his head. He set the golden plate, the holy crown, on the front of the turban, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.right_text: Moses also put the turban on Aaron’s head and set the gold plate, the holy diadem, on the front of the turban, as the LORD had commanded him.

units.left_text: Moses took the anointing oil, and anointed the tabernacle and all that was in it, and sanctified them.
units.right_text: Next, Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it; and so he consecrated them.

units.left_text: He sprinkled it on the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its vessels, and the basin and its base, to sanctify them.
units.right_text: He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times, anointing the altar and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand, to consecrate them.

units.left_text: He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, and anointed him, to sanctify him.
units.right_text: He also poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him to consecrate him.

units.left_text: Moses brought Aaron’s sons, and clothed them with tunics, and tied sashes on them, and put headbands on them, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.right_text: Then Moses presented Aaron’s sons, put tunics on them, wrapped sashes around them, and tied headbands on them, just as the LORD had commanded him.

units.left_text: He brought the bull of the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull of the sin offering.
units.right_text: Moses then brought the bull near for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

units.left_text: He killed it; and Moses took the blood, and put it around on the horns of the altar with his finger, and purified the altar, and poured out the blood at the base of the altar, and sanctified it, to make atonement for it.
units.right_text: Moses slaughtered the bull, took some of the blood, and applied it with his finger to all four horns of the altar, purifying the altar. He poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar and consecrated it so that atonement could be made on it.

units.left_text: He took all the fat that was on the innards, and the cover of the liver, and the two kidneys, and their fat; and Moses burned it on the altar.
units.right_text: Moses also took all the fat that was on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys and their fat, and burned it all on the altar.

units.left_text: But the bull, and its skin, and its meat, and its dung, he burned with fire outside the camp, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.right_text: But the bull with its hide, flesh, and dung he burned outside the camp, as the LORD had commanded him.

units.left_text: He presented the ram of the burnt offering. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the ram.
units.right_text: Then Moses presented the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

units.left_text: He killed it; and Moses sprinkled the blood around on the altar.
units.right_text: Moses slaughtered the ram and splattered the blood on all sides of the altar.

units.left_text: He cut the ram into its pieces; and Moses burned the head, and the pieces, and the fat.
units.right_text: He cut the ram into pieces and burned the head, the pieces, and the fat.

units.left_text: He washed the innards and the legs with water; and Moses burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering for a pleasant aroma. It was an offering made by fire to the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.right_text: He washed the entrails and legs with water and burned the entire ram on the altar as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

units.left_text: He presented the other ram, the ram of consecration. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the ram.
units.right_text: After that, Moses presented the other ram, the ram of ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

units.left_text: He killed it; and Moses took some of its blood, and put it on the tip of Aaron’s right ear, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot.
units.right_text: Moses slaughtered the ram and took some of its blood and put it on Aaron’s right earlobe, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

units.left_text: He brought Aaron’s sons; and Moses put some of the blood on the tip of their right ear, and on the thumb of their right hand, and on the great toe of their right foot; and Moses sprinkled the blood around on the altar.
units.right_text: Moses also presented Aaron’s sons and put some of the blood on their right earlobes, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then he splattered the blood on all sides of the altar.

units.left_text: He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat that was on the innards, the cover of the liver, the two kidneys and their fat, and the right thigh;
units.right_text: And Moses took the fat— the fat tail, all the fat that was on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys with their fat— as well as the right thigh.

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

units.left_text: “When you have come into the land of Canaan, which I give to you for a possession, and I put a spreading mildew in a house in the land of your possession,
units.right_text: “When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as your possession, and I put a contamination of mildew into a house in that land,

units.left_text: then he who owns the house shall come and tell the priest, saying, ‘There seems to me to be some sort of plague in the house.’
units.right_text: the owner of the house shall come and tell the priest, ‘Something like mildew has appeared in my house.’

units.left_text: The priest shall command that they empty the house, before the priest goes in to examine the plague, that all that is in the house not be made unclean. Afterward the priest shall go in to inspect the house.
units.right_text: The priest must order that the house be cleared before he enters it to examine the mildew, so that nothing in the house will become unclean. After this, the priest shall go in to inspect the house.

units.left_text: He shall examine the plague; and behold, if the plague is in the walls of the house with hollow streaks, greenish or reddish, and it appears to be deeper than the wall,
units.right_text: He is to examine the house, and if the mildew on the walls consists of green or red depressions that appear to be beneath the surface of the wall,

units.left_text: then the priest shall go out of the house to the door of the house, and shut up the house seven days.
units.right_text: the priest shall go outside the doorway of the house and close it up for seven days.

units.left_text: The priest shall come again on the seventh day, and look. If the plague has spread in the walls of the house,
units.right_text: On the seventh day the priest is to return and inspect the house. If the mildew has spread on the walls,

units.left_text: then the priest shall command that they take out the stones in which is the plague, and cast them into an unclean place outside of the city.
units.right_text: he must order that the contaminated stones be pulled out and thrown into an unclean place outside the city.

units.left_text: He shall cause the inside of the house to be scraped all over. They shall pour out the mortar that they scraped off outside of the city into an unclean place.
units.right_text: And he shall have the inside of the house scraped completely and the plaster that is scraped off dumped into an unclean place outside the city.

units.left_text: They shall take other stones, and put them in the place of those stones; and he shall take other mortar, and shall plaster the house.
units.right_text: So different stones must be obtained to replace the contaminated ones, as well as additional mortar to replaster the house.

units.left_text: “If the plague comes again, and breaks out in the house after he has taken out the stones, and after he has scraped the house, and after it was plastered,
units.right_text: If the mildew reappears in the house after the stones have been torn out and the house has been scraped and replastered,

units.left_text: then the priest shall come in and look; and behold, if the plague has spread in the house, it is a destructive mildew in the house. It is unclean.
units.right_text: the priest must come and inspect it.

units.left_text: He shall break down the house, its stones, and its timber, and all the house’s mortar. He shall carry them out of the city into an unclean place.
units.right_text: It must be torn down with its stones, its timbers, and all its plaster, and taken outside the city to an unclean place.

units.left_text: “Moreover he who goes into the house while it is shut up shall be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: Anyone who enters the house during any of the days that it is closed up will be unclean until evening.

units.left_text: He who lies down in the house shall wash his clothes; and he who eats in the house shall wash his clothes.
units.right_text: And anyone who sleeps in the house or eats in it must wash his clothes.

units.left_text: “If the priest shall come in, and examine it, and behold, the plague hasn’t spread in the house, after the house was plastered, then the priest shall pronounce the house clean, because the plague is healed.
units.right_text: If, however, the priest comes and inspects it, and the mildew has not spread after the house has been replastered, he shall pronounce the house clean, because the mildew is gone.

units.left_text: To cleanse the house he shall take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop.
units.right_text: He is to take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop to purify the house;

units.left_text: He shall kill one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running water.
units.right_text: and he shall slaughter one of the birds over fresh water in a clay pot.

units.left_text: He shall take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet, and the living bird, and dip them in the blood of the slain bird, and in the running water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
units.right_text: Then he shall take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet yarn, and the live bird, dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.

units.left_text: He shall cleanse the house with the blood of the bird, and with the running water, with the living bird, with the cedar wood, with the hyssop, and with the scarlet;
units.right_text: And he shall cleanse the house with the bird’s blood, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the scarlet yarn.

units.left_text: but he shall let the living bird go out of the city into the open field. So shall he make atonement for the house; and it shall be clean.”
units.right_text: Finally, he is to release the live bird into the open fields outside the city. In this way he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean.

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
units.right_text: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

units.left_text: “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘When any man has a discharge from his body, because of his discharge he is unclean.
units.right_text: “Say to the Israelites, ‘When any man has a bodily discharge, the discharge is unclean.

units.left_text: This shall be his uncleanness in his discharge: whether his body runs with his discharge, or his body has stopped from his discharge, it is his uncleanness.
units.right_text: This uncleanness is from his discharge, whether his body allows the discharge to flow or blocks it. So his discharge will bring about uncleanness.

units.left_text: “‘Every bed on which he who has the discharge lies shall be unclean; and everything he sits on shall be unclean.
units.right_text: Any bed on which the man with the discharge lies will be unclean, and any furniture on which he sits will be unclean.

units.left_text: Whoever touches his bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.

units.left_text: He who sits on anything on which the man who has the discharge sat shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: Whoever sits on furniture on which the man with the discharge was sitting must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.

units.left_text: “‘He who touches the body of him who has the discharge shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: Whoever touches the body of the man with a discharge must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.

units.left_text: “‘If he who has the discharge spits on him who is clean, then he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: If the man with the discharge spits on one who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.

units.left_text: “‘Whatever saddle he who has the discharge rides on shall be unclean.
units.right_text: Any saddle on which the man with the discharge rides will be unclean.

units.left_text: Whoever touches anything that was under him shall be unclean until the evening. He who carries those things shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: Whoever touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.

units.left_text: “‘Whomever he who has the discharge touches, without having rinsed his hands in water, he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: If the man with the discharge touches anyone without first rinsing his hands with water, the one who was touched must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.

units.left_text: “‘The earthen vessel, which he who has the discharge touches, shall be broken; and every vessel of wood shall be rinsed in water.
units.right_text: Any clay pot that the man with the discharge touches must be broken, and any wooden utensil must be rinsed with water.

units.left_text: “‘When he who has a discharge is cleansed of his discharge, then he shall count to himself seven days for his cleansing, and wash his clothes; and he shall bathe his flesh in running water, and shall be clean.
units.right_text: When the man has been cleansed from his discharge, he must count off seven days for his cleansing, wash his clothes, and bathe himself in fresh water, and he shall be clean.

units.left_text: “‘On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, and come before the LORD to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and give them to the priest.
units.right_text: On the eighth day he is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, come before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and give them to the priest.

units.left_text: The priest shall offer them, the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD for his discharge.
units.right_text: The priest is to sacrifice them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for the man before the LORD because of his discharge.

units.left_text: “‘If any man has an emission of semen, then he shall bathe all his flesh in water, and be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body with water, and he will be unclean until evening.

units.left_text: Every garment and every skin which the semen is on shall be washed with water, and be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: Any clothing or leather on which there is an emission of semen must be washed with water, and it will remain unclean until evening.

units.left_text: If a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, they shall both bathe themselves in water, and be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: If a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both must bathe with water, and they will remain unclean until evening.

units.left_text: “‘If a woman has a discharge, and her discharge in her flesh is blood, she shall be in her impurity seven days. Whoever touches her shall be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: When a woman has a discharge consisting of blood from her body, she will be unclean due to her menstruation for seven days, and anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.

units.left_text: “‘Everything that she lies on in her impurity shall be unclean. Everything also that she sits on shall be unclean.
units.right_text: Anything on which she lies or sits during her menstruation will be unclean,

units.left_text: Whoever touches her bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: and anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.

units.left_text: Whoever touches anything that she sits on shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: Whoever touches any furniture on which she was sitting must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.

units.left_text: If it is on the bed, or on anything she sits on, when he touches it, he shall be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: And whether it is a bed or furniture on which she was sitting, whoever touches it will be unclean until evening.

units.left_text: “‘If any man lies with her, and her monthly flow is on him, he shall be unclean seven days; and every bed he lies on shall be unclean.
units.right_text: If a man lies with her and her menstrual flow touches him, he will be unclean for seven days, and any bed on which he lies will become unclean.

units.left_text: “‘If a woman has a discharge of her blood many days not in the time of her period, or if she has a discharge beyond the time of her period, all the days of the discharge of her uncleanness shall be as in the days of her period. She is unclean.
units.right_text: When a woman has a discharge of her blood for many days at a time other than her menstrual period, or if it continues beyond her period, she will be unclean all the days of her unclean discharge, just as she is during the days of her menstruation.

units.left_text: Every bed she lies on all the days of her discharge shall be to her as the bed of her period. Everything she sits on shall be unclean, as the uncleanness of her period.
units.right_text: Any bed on which she lies or any furniture on which she sits during the days of her discharge will be unclean, like her bed during her menstrual period.

units.left_text: Whoever touches these things shall be unclean, and shall wash his clothes and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
units.right_text: Anyone who touches these things will be unclean; he must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.

units.left_text: “‘But if she is cleansed of her discharge, then she shall count to herself seven days, and after that she shall be clean.
units.right_text: When a woman is cleansed of her discharge, she must count off seven days, and after that she will be ceremonially clean.

units.left_text: On the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, and bring them to the priest, to the door of the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: On the eighth day she is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

units.left_text: The priest shall offer the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering; and the priest shall make atonement for her before the LORD for the uncleanness of her discharge.
units.right_text: The priest is to sacrifice one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for her before the LORD for her unclean discharge.

units.left_text: “‘Thus you shall separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, so they will not die in their uncleanness when they defile my tabernacle that is among them.’”
units.right_text: You must keep the children of Israel separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die by defiling My tabernacle, which is among them.

units.left_text: This is the law of him who has a discharge, and of him who has an emission of semen, so that he is unclean by it;
units.right_text: This is the law of him who has a discharge, of the man who has an emission of semen whereby he is unclean,

units.left_text: and of her who has her period, and of a man or woman who has a discharge, and of him who lies with her who is unclean.
units.right_text: of a woman in her menstrual period, of any male or female who has a discharge, and of a man who lies with an unclean woman.’”

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they came near before the LORD, and died;
units.right_text: Now the LORD spoke to Moses after the death of two of Aaron’s sons when they approached the presence of the LORD.

units.left_text: and the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron your brother not to come at just any time into the Most Holy Place within the veil, before the mercy seat which is on the ark; lest he die; for I will appear in the cloud on the mercy seat.
