units.right_text: You are to have the same standard of law for the foreign resident and the native; for I am the LORD your God.’”

units.left_text: Moses spoke to the children of Israel; and they brought him who had cursed out of the camp, and stoned him with stones. The children of Israel did as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.right_text: Then Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they took the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him. So the Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses.

units.left_text: The LORD said to Moses on Mount Sinai,
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses on Mount Sinai,

units.left_text: “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘When you come into the land which I give you, then the land shall keep a Sabbath to the LORD.
units.right_text: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land that I am giving you, the land itself must observe a Sabbath to the LORD.

units.left_text: You shall sow your field six years, and you shall prune your vineyard six years, and gather in its fruits;
units.right_text: For six years you may sow your field and prune your vineyard and gather its crops.

units.left_text: but in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of solemn rest for the land, a Sabbath to the LORD. You shall not sow your field or prune your vineyard.
units.right_text: But in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land — a Sabbath to the LORD.

units.left_text: What grows of itself in your harvest you shall not reap, and you shall not gather the grapes of your undressed vine. It shall be a year of solemn rest for the land.
units.right_text: You are not to reap the aftergrowth of your harvest or gather the grapes of your untended vines. The land must have a year of complete rest.

units.left_text: The Sabbath of the land shall be for food for you; for yourself, for your servant, for your maid, for your hired servant, and for your stranger, who lives as a foreigner with you.
units.right_text: Whatever the land yields during the Sabbath year shall be food for you— for yourself, your manservant and maidservant, the hired hand or foreigner who stays with you,

units.left_text: For your livestock also, and for the animals that are in your land, shall all its increase be for food.
units.right_text: and for your livestock and the wild animals in your land. All its growth may serve as food.

units.left_text: “‘You shall count off seven Sabbaths of years, seven times seven years; and there shall be to you the days of seven Sabbaths of years, even forty-nine years.
units.right_text: And you shall count off seven Sabbaths of years — seven times seven years — so that the seven Sabbaths of years amount to forty-nine years.

units.left_text: Then you shall sound the loud trumpet on the tenth day of the seventh month. On the Day of Atonement you shall sound the trumpet throughout all your land.
units.right_text: Then you are to sound the horn far and wide on the tenth day of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement. You shall sound it throughout your land.

units.left_text: You shall make the fiftieth year holy, and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee to you; and each of you shall return to his own property, and each of you shall return to his family.
units.right_text: So you are to consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty in the land for all its inhabitants. It shall be your Jubilee, when each of you is to return to his property and to his clan.

units.left_text: That fiftieth year shall be a jubilee to you. In it you shall not sow, neither reap that which grows of itself, nor gather from the undressed vines.
units.right_text: The fiftieth year will be a Jubilee for you; you are not to sow the land or reap its aftergrowth or harvest the untended vines.

units.left_text: For it is a jubilee; it shall be holy to you. You shall eat of its increase out of the field.
units.right_text: For it is a Jubilee; it shall be holy to you. You may eat only the crops taken directly from the field.

units.left_text: “‘In this Year of Jubilee each of you shall return to his property.
units.right_text: In this Year of Jubilee, each of you shall return to his own property.

units.left_text: “‘If you sell anything to your neighbor, or buy from your neighbor, you shall not wrong one another.
units.right_text: If you make a sale to your neighbor or a purchase from him, you must not take advantage of each other.

units.left_text: According to the number of years after the Jubilee you shall buy from your neighbor. According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you.
units.right_text: You are to buy from your neighbor according to the number of years since the last Jubilee; he is to sell to you according to the number of harvest years remaining.

units.left_text: According to the length of the years you shall increase its price, and according to the shortness of the years you shall diminish its price; for he is selling the number of the crops to you.
units.right_text: You shall increase the price in proportion to a greater number of years, or decrease it in proportion to a lesser number of years; for he is selling you a given number of harvests.

units.left_text: You shall not wrong one another, but you shall fear your God; for I am the LORD your God.
units.right_text: Do not take advantage of each other, but fear your God; for I am the LORD your God.

units.left_text: “‘Therefore you shall do my statutes, and keep my ordinances and do them; and you shall dwell in the land in safety.
units.right_text: You are to keep My statutes and carefully observe My judgments, so that you may dwell securely in the land.

units.left_text: The land shall yield its fruit, and you shall eat your fill, and dwell therein in safety.
units.right_text: Then the land will yield its fruit, so that you can eat your fill and dwell in safety in the land.

units.left_text: If you said, “What shall we eat the seventh year? Behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase;”
units.right_text: Now you may wonder, ‘What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow or gather our produce?’

units.left_text: then I will command my blessing on you in the sixth year, and it shall bear fruit for the three years.
units.right_text: But I will send My blessing upon you in the sixth year, so that the land will yield a crop sufficient for three years.

units.left_text: You shall sow the eighth year, and eat of the fruits from the old store until the ninth year. Until its fruits come in, you shall eat the old store.
units.right_text: While you are sowing in the eighth year, you will be eating from the previous harvest, until the ninth year’s harvest comes in.

units.left_text: “‘The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is mine; for you are strangers and live as foreigners with me.
units.right_text: The land must not be sold permanently, because it is Mine, and you are but foreigners and residents with Me.

units.left_text: In all the land of your possession you shall grant a redemption for the land.
units.right_text: Thus for every piece of property you possess, you must provide for the redemption of the land.

units.left_text: “‘If your brother becomes poor, and sells some of his possessions, then his kinsman who is next to him shall come, and redeem that which his brother has sold.
units.right_text: If your brother becomes impoverished and sells some of his property, his nearest of kin may come and redeem what his brother has sold.

units.left_text: If a man has no one to redeem it, and he becomes prosperous and finds sufficient means to redeem it,
units.right_text: Or if a man has no one to redeem it for him, but he prospers and acquires enough to redeem his land,

units.left_text: then let him reckon the years since its sale, and restore the surplus to the man to whom he sold it; and he shall return to his property.
units.right_text: he shall calculate the years since its sale, repay the balance to the man to whom he sold it, and return to his property.

units.left_text: But if he isn’t able to get it back for himself, then what he has sold shall remain in the hand of him who has bought it until the Year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee it shall be released, and he shall return to his property.
units.right_text: But if he cannot obtain enough to repay him, what he sold will remain in possession of the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee, however, it is to be released, so that he may return to his property.

units.left_text: “‘If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, then he may redeem it within a whole year after it has been sold. For a full year he shall have the right of redemption.
units.right_text: If a man sells a house in a walled city, he retains his right of redemption until a full year after its sale; during that year it may be redeemed.

units.left_text: If it isn’t redeemed within the space of a full year, then the house that is in the walled city shall be made sure in perpetuity to him who bought it, throughout his generations. It shall not be released in the Jubilee.
units.right_text: If it is not redeemed by the end of a full year, then the house in the walled city is permanently transferred to its buyer and his descendants. It is not to be released in the Jubilee.

units.left_text: But the houses of the villages which have no wall around them shall be accounted for with the fields of the country: they may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee.
units.right_text: But houses in villages with no walls around them are to be considered as open fields. They may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee.

units.left_text: “‘Nevertheless, in the cities of the Levites, the Levites may redeem the houses in the cities of their possession at any time.
units.right_text: As for the cities of the Levites, the Levites always have the right to redeem their houses in the cities they possess.

units.left_text: The Levites may redeem the house that was sold, and the city of his possession, and it shall be released in the Jubilee; for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel.
units.right_text: So whatever belongs to the Levites may be redeemed— a house sold in a city they possess— and must be released in the Jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the Israelites.

units.left_text: But the field of the pasture lands of their cities may not be sold, for it is their perpetual possession.
units.right_text: But the open pastureland around their cities may not be sold, for this is their permanent possession.

units.left_text: “‘If your brother has become poor, and his hand can’t support himself among you, then you shall uphold him. He shall live with you like an alien and a temporary resident.
units.right_text: Now if your countryman becomes destitute and cannot support himself among you, then you are to help him as you would a foreigner or stranger, so that he can continue to live among you.

units.left_text: Take no interest from him or profit; but fear your God, that your brother may live among you.
units.right_text: Do not take any interest or profit from him, but fear your God, that your countryman may live among you.

units.left_text: You shall not lend him your money at interest, nor give him your food for profit.
units.right_text: You must not lend him your silver at interest or sell him your food for profit.

units.left_text: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God.
units.right_text: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.

units.left_text: “‘If your brother has grown poor among you, and sells himself to you, you shall not make him to serve as a slave.
units.right_text: If a countryman among you becomes destitute and sells himself to you, then you must not force him into slave labor.

units.left_text: As a hired servant, and as a temporary resident, he shall be with you; he shall serve with you until the Year of Jubilee.
units.right_text: Let him stay with you as a hired worker or temporary resident; he is to work for you until the Year of Jubilee.

units.left_text: Then he shall go out from you, he and his children with him, and shall return to his own family, and to the possession of his fathers.
units.right_text: Then he and his children are to be released, and he may return to his clan and to the property of his fathers.

units.left_text: For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They shall not be sold as slaves.
units.right_text: Because the Israelites are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt, they are not to be sold as slaves.

units.left_text: You shall not rule over him with harshness, but shall fear your God.
units.right_text: You are not to rule over them harshly, but you shall fear your God.

units.left_text: “‘As for your male and your female slaves, whom you may have from the nations that are around you, from them you may buy male and female slaves.
units.right_text: Your menservants and maidservants shall come from the nations around you, from whom you may purchase them.

units.left_text: Moreover, of the children of the aliens who live among you, of them you may buy, and of their families who are with you, which they have conceived in your land; and they will be your property.
units.right_text: You may also purchase them from the foreigners residing among you or their clans living among you who are born in your land. These may become your property.

units.left_text: You may make them an inheritance for your children after you, to hold for a possession. Of them you may take your slaves forever, but over your brothers the children of Israel you shall not rule, one over another, with harshness.
units.right_text: You may leave them to your sons after you to inherit as property; you can make them slaves for life. But as for your brothers, the Israelites, no man may rule harshly over his brother.

units.left_text: “‘If an alien or temporary resident with you becomes rich, and your brother beside him has grown poor, and sells himself to the stranger or foreigner living among you, or to a member of the stranger’s family,
units.right_text: If a foreigner residing among you prospers, but your countryman dwelling near him becomes destitute and sells himself to the foreigner or to a member of his clan,

units.left_text: after he is sold he may be redeemed. One of his brothers may redeem him;
units.right_text: he retains the right of redemption after he has sold himself. One of his brothers may redeem him:

units.left_text: or his uncle, or his uncle’s son, may redeem him, or any who is a close relative to him of his family may redeem him; or if he has grown rich, he may redeem himself.
units.right_text: either his uncle or cousin or any close relative from his clan may redeem him. Or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.

units.left_text: He shall reckon with him who bought him from the year that he sold himself to him to the Year of Jubilee. The price of his sale shall be according to the number of years; he shall be with him according to the time of a hired servant.
units.right_text: He and his purchaser will then count the time from the year he sold himself up to the Year of Jubilee. The price of his sale will be determined by the number of years, based on the daily wages of a hired hand.

units.left_text: If there are yet many years, according to them he shall give back the price of his redemption out of the money that he was bought for.
units.right_text: If many years remain, he must pay for his redemption in proportion to his purchase price.

units.left_text: If there remain but a few years to the year of jubilee, then he shall reckon with him; according to his years of service he shall give back the price of his redemption.
units.right_text: If only a few years remain until the Year of Jubilee, he is to calculate and pay his redemption according to his remaining years.

units.left_text: As a servant hired year by year shall he be with him. He shall not rule with harshness over him in your sight.
units.right_text: He shall be treated like a man hired from year to year, but a foreign owner must not rule over him harshly in your sight.

units.left_text: If he isn’t redeemed by these means, then he shall be released in the Year of Jubilee: he and his children with him.
units.right_text: Even if he is not redeemed in any of these ways, he and his children shall be released in the Year of Jubilee.

units.left_text: For to me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
units.right_text: For the Israelites are My servants. They are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.[’’]

units.left_text: “‘You shall make for yourselves no idols, and you shall not raise up a carved image or a pillar, and you shall not place any figured stone in your land, to bow down to it; for I am the LORD your God.
units.right_text: “You must not make idols for yourselves or set up a carved image or sacred pillar; you must not place a sculpted stone in your land to bow down to it. For I am the LORD your God.

units.left_text: “‘You shall keep my Sabbaths, and have reverence for my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
units.right_text: You must keep My Sabbaths and have reverence for My sanctuary. I am the LORD.

units.left_text: “‘If you walk in my statutes and keep my commandments, and do them,
units.right_text: If you follow My statutes and carefully keep My commandments,

units.left_text: then I will give you your rains in their season, and the land shall yield its increase, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit.
units.right_text: I will give you rains in their season, and the land will yield its produce, and the trees of the field will bear their fruit.

units.left_text: Your threshing shall continue until the vintage, and the vintage shall continue until the sowing time. You shall eat your bread to the full, and dwell in your land safely.
units.right_text: Your threshing will continue until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will continue until sowing time; you will have your fill of food to eat and will dwell securely in your land.

units.left_text: “‘I will give peace in the land, and you shall lie down, and no one will make you afraid. I will remove evil animals out of the land, neither shall the sword go through your land.
units.right_text: And I will give peace to the land, and you will lie down with nothing to fear. I will rid the land of dangerous animals, and no sword will pass through your land.

units.left_text: You shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword.
units.right_text: You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall by the sword before you.

units.left_text: Five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall chase ten thousand; and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
units.right_text: Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand, and your enemies will fall by the sword before you.

units.left_text: “‘I will have respect for you, make you fruitful, multiply you, and will establish my covenant with you.
units.right_text: I will turn toward you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will establish My covenant with you.

units.left_text: You shall eat old supplies long kept, and you shall move out the old because of the new.
units.right_text: You will still be eating the old supply of grain when you need to clear it out to make room for the new.

units.left_text: I will set my tent among you, and my soul won’t abhor you.
units.right_text: And I will make My dwelling place among you, and My soul will not despise you.

units.left_text: I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you will be my people.
units.right_text: I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be My people.

units.left_text: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that you should not be their slaves. I have broken the bars of your yoke, and made you walk upright.
units.right_text: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be slaves to the Egyptians. I broke the bars of your yoke and enabled you to walk in uprightness.

units.left_text: “‘But if you will not listen to me, and will not do all these commandments,
units.right_text: If, however, you fail to obey Me and to carry out all these commandments,

units.left_text: and if you shall reject my statutes, and if your soul abhors my ordinances, so that you will not do all my commandments, but break my covenant,
units.right_text: and if you reject My statutes, despise My ordinances, and neglect to carry out all My commandments, and so break My covenant,

units.left_text: I also will do this to you: I will appoint terror over you, even consumption and fever, that shall consume the eyes, and make the soul to pine away. You will sow your seed in vain, for your enemies will eat it.
units.right_text: then this is what I will do to you: I will bring upon you sudden terror, wasting disease, and fever that will destroy your sight and drain your life. You will sow your seed in vain, because your enemies will eat it.

units.left_text: I will set my face against you, and you will be struck before your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you; and you will flee when no one pursues you.
units.right_text: And I will set My face against you, so that you will be defeated by your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee when no one pursues you.

units.left_text: “‘If you in spite of these things will not listen to me, then I will chastise you seven times more for your sins.
units.right_text: And if after all this you will not obey Me, I will proceed to punish you sevenfold for your sins.

units.left_text: I will break the pride of your power, and I will make your sky like iron, and your soil like bronze.
units.right_text: I will break down your stubborn pride and make your sky like iron and your land like bronze,

units.left_text: Your strength will be spent in vain; for your land won’t yield its increase, neither will the trees of the land yield their fruit.
units.right_text: and your strength will be spent in vain. For your land will not yield its produce, and the trees of the land will not bear their fruit.

units.left_text: “‘If you walk contrary to me, and won’t listen to me, then I will bring seven times more plagues on you according to your sins.
units.right_text: If you walk in hostility toward Me and refuse to obey Me, I will multiply your plagues seven times, according to your sins.

units.left_text: I will send the wild animals among you, which will rob you of your children, destroy your livestock, and make you few in number. Your roads will become desolate.
units.right_text: I will send wild animals against you to rob you of your children, destroy your livestock, and reduce your numbers, until your roads lie desolate.

units.left_text: “‘If by these things you won’t be turned back to me, but will walk contrary to me,
units.right_text: And if in spite of these things you do not accept My discipline, but continue to walk in hostility toward Me,

units.left_text: then I will also walk contrary to you; and I will strike you, even I, seven times for your sins.
units.right_text: then I will act with hostility toward you, and I will strike you sevenfold for your sins.

units.left_text: I will bring a sword upon you that will execute the vengeance of the covenant. You will be gathered together within your cities, and I will send the pestilence among you. You will be delivered into the hand of the enemy.
units.right_text: And I will bring a sword against you to execute the vengeance of the covenant. Though you withdraw into your cities, I will send a plague among you, and you will be delivered into the hand of the enemy.

units.left_text: When I break your staff of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven, and they shall deliver your bread again by weight. You shall eat, and not be satisfied.
units.right_text: When I cut off your supply of bread, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven and dole out your bread by weight, so that you will eat but not be satisfied.

units.left_text: “‘If you in spite of this won’t listen to me, but walk contrary to me,
units.right_text: But if in spite of all this you do not obey Me, but continue to walk in hostility toward Me,

units.left_text: then I will walk contrary to you in wrath. I will also chastise you seven times for your sins.
units.right_text: then I will walk in fury against you, and I, even I, will punish you sevenfold for your sins.

units.left_text: You will eat the flesh of your sons, and you will eat the flesh of your daughters.
units.right_text: You will eat the flesh of your own sons and daughters.

units.left_text: I will destroy your high places, and cut down your incense altars, and cast your dead bodies upon the bodies of your idols; and my soul will abhor you.
units.right_text: I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars, and heap your lifeless bodies on the lifeless remains of your idols; and My soul will despise you.

units.left_text: I will lay your cities waste, and will bring your sanctuaries to desolation. I will not take delight in the sweet fragrance of your offerings.
units.right_text: I will reduce your cities to rubble and lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will refuse to smell the pleasing aroma of your sacrifices.

units.left_text: I will bring the land into desolation, and your enemies who dwell in it will be astonished at it.
units.right_text: And I will lay waste the land, so that your enemies who dwell in it will be appalled.

units.left_text: I will scatter you among the nations, and I will draw out the sword after you. Your land will be a desolation, and your cities shall be a waste.
units.right_text: But I will scatter you among the nations and will draw out a sword after you as your land becomes desolate and your cities are laid waste.

units.left_text: Then the land will enjoy its Sabbaths as long as it lies desolate and you are in your enemies’ land. Even then the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
units.right_text: Then the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths all the days it lies desolate, while you are in the land of your enemies. At that time the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.

units.left_text: As long as it lies desolate it shall have rest, even the rest which it didn’t have in your Sabbaths when you lived on it.
units.right_text: As long as it lies desolate, the land will have the rest it did not receive during the Sabbaths when you lived in it.

units.left_text: “‘As for those of you who are left, I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a driven leaf will put them to flight; and they shall flee, as one flees from the sword. They will fall when no one pursues.
units.right_text: As for those of you who survive, I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, so that even the sound of a windblown leaf will put them to flight. And they will flee as one flees the sword, and fall when no one pursues them.

units.left_text: They will stumble over one another, as it were before the sword, when no one pursues. You will have no power to stand before your enemies.
units.right_text: They will stumble over one another as before the sword, though no one is behind them. So you will not be able to stand against your enemies.

units.left_text: You will perish among the nations. The land of your enemies will eat you up.
units.right_text: You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will consume you.

units.left_text: Those of you who are left will pine away in their iniquity in your enemies’ lands; and also in the iniquities of their fathers they shall pine away with them.
units.right_text: Those of you who survive in the lands of your enemies will waste away in their iniquity and will decay in the sins of their fathers.

units.left_text: “‘If they confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers, in their trespass which they trespassed against me; and also that because they walked contrary to me,
units.right_text: But if they will confess their iniquity and that of their fathers in the unfaithfulness that they practiced against Me, by which they have also walked in hostility toward Me—

units.left_text: I also walked contrary to them, and brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled, and they then accept the punishment of their iniquity,
units.right_text: and I acted with hostility toward them and brought them into the land of their enemies— and if their uncircumcised hearts will be humbled and they will make amends for their iniquity,

units.left_text: then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham; and I will remember the land.
units.right_text: then I will remember My covenant with Jacob and My covenant with Isaac and My covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.

units.left_text: The land also will be left by them, and will enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them; and they will accept the punishment of their iniquity because they rejected my ordinances, and their soul abhorred my statutes.
units.right_text: For the land will be abandoned by them, and it will enjoy its Sabbaths by lying desolate without them. And they will pay the penalty for their iniquity, because they rejected My ordinances and abhorred My statutes.

units.left_text: Yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly and to break my covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God.
units.right_text: Yet in spite of this, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject or despise them so as to destroy them and break My covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God.

units.left_text: But I will for their sake remember the covenant of their ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God. I am the LORD.’”
units.right_text: But for their sake I will remember the covenant with their fathers, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God. I am the LORD.”

units.left_text: These are the statutes, ordinances, and laws, which the LORD made between him and the children of Israel in Mount Sinai by Moses.
units.right_text: These are the statutes, ordinances, and laws that the LORD established between Himself and the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.left_text: “Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them, ‘When a man consecrates a person to the LORD in a vow, according to your valuation,
units.right_text: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them, ‘When someone makes a special vow to the LORD involving the value of persons,

units.left_text: your valuation of a male from twenty years old to sixty years old shall be fifty shekels of silver, according to the shekel of the sanctuary.
units.right_text: if the valuation concerns a male from twenty to sixty years of age, then your valuation shall be fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel.

units.left_text: If she is a female, then your valuation shall be thirty shekels.
units.right_text: Or if it is a female, then your valuation shall be thirty shekels.

units.left_text: If the person is from five years old to twenty years old, then your valuation shall be for a male twenty shekels, and for a female ten shekels.
units.right_text: And if the person is from five to twenty years of age, then your valuation for the male shall be twenty shekels, and for the female ten shekels.

units.left_text: If the person is from a month old to five years old, then your valuation shall be for a male five shekels of silver, and for a female your valuation shall be three shekels of silver.
units.right_text: Now if the person is from one month to five years of age, then your valuation for the male shall be five shekels of silver, and for the female three shekels of silver.

units.left_text: If the person is from sixty years old and upward; if he is a male, then your valuation shall be fifteen shekels, and for a female ten shekels.
units.right_text: And if the person is sixty years of age or older, then your valuation shall be fifteen shekels for the male and ten shekels for the female.

units.left_text: But if he is poorer than your valuation, then he shall be set before the priest, and the priest shall assign a value to him. The priest shall assign a value according to his ability to pay.
units.right_text: But if the one making the vow is too poor to pay the valuation, he is to present the person before the priest, who shall set the value according to what the one making the vow can afford.

units.left_text: “‘If it is an animal of which men offer an offering to the LORD, all that any man gives of such to the LORD becomes holy.
units.right_text: If he vows an animal that may be brought as an offering to the LORD, any such animal given to the LORD shall be holy.

units.left_text: He shall not alter it, nor exchange it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good. If he shall at all exchange animal for animal, then both it and that for which it is exchanged shall be holy.
units.right_text: He must not replace it or exchange it, either good for bad or bad for good. But if he does substitute one animal for another, both that animal and its substitute will be holy.

units.left_text: If it is any unclean animal, of which they do not offer as an offering to the LORD, then he shall set the animal before the priest;
units.right_text: But if the vow involves any of the unclean animals that may not be brought as an offering to the LORD, the animal must be presented before the priest.

units.left_text: and the priest shall evaluate it, whether it is good or bad. As the priest evaluates it, so it shall be.
units.right_text: The priest shall set its value, whether high or low; as the priest values it, the price will be set.

units.left_text: But if he will indeed redeem it, then he shall add the fifth part of it to its valuation.
units.right_text: If, however, the owner decides to redeem the animal, he must add a fifth to its value.

units.left_text: “‘When a man dedicates his house to be holy to the LORD, then the priest shall evaluate it, whether it is good or bad. As the priest evaluates it, so it shall stand.
units.right_text: Now if a man consecrates his house as holy to the LORD, then the priest shall value it either as good or bad. The price will stand just as the priest values it.

units.left_text: If he who dedicates it will redeem his house, then he shall add the fifth part of the money of your valuation to it, and it shall be his.
units.right_text: But if he who consecrated his house redeems it, he must add a fifth to the assessed value, and it will belong to him.

units.left_text: “‘If a man dedicates to the LORD part of the field of his possession, then your valuation shall be according to the seed for it. The sowing of a homer of barley shall be valued at fifty shekels of silver.
units.right_text: If a man consecrates to the LORD a parcel of his land, then your valuation shall be proportional to the seed required for it — fifty shekels of silver for every homer of barley seed.

units.left_text: If he dedicates his field from the Year of Jubilee, according to your valuation it shall stand.
units.right_text: If he consecrates his field during the Year of Jubilee, the price will stand according to your valuation.

units.left_text: But if he dedicates his field after the Jubilee, then the priest shall reckon to him the money according to the years that remain to the Year of Jubilee; and an abatement shall be made from your valuation.
units.right_text: But if he consecrates his field after the Jubilee, the priest is to calculate the price in proportion to the years left until the next Year of Jubilee, so that your valuation will be reduced.

units.left_text: If he who dedicated the field will indeed redeem it, then he shall add the fifth part of the money of your valuation to it, and it shall remain his.
units.right_text: And if the one who consecrated the field decides to redeem it, he must add a fifth to the assessed value, and it shall belong to him.

units.left_text: If he will not redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed any more;
units.right_text: If, however, he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold it to another man, it may no longer be redeemed.

units.left_text: but the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy to the LORD, as a devoted field. It shall be owned by the priests.
units.right_text: When the field is released in the Jubilee, it will become holy, like a field devoted to the LORD; it becomes the property of the priests.

units.left_text: “‘If he dedicates a field to the LORD which he has bought, which is not of the field of his possession,
units.right_text: Now if a man consecrates to the LORD a field he has purchased, which is not a part of his own property,

units.left_text: then the priest shall reckon to him the worth of your valuation up to the Year of Jubilee; and he shall give your valuation on that day, as a holy thing to the LORD.
units.right_text: then the priest shall calculate for him the value up to the Year of Jubilee, and the man shall pay the assessed value on that day as a sacred offering to the LORD.

units.left_text: In the Year of Jubilee the field shall return to him from whom it was bought, even to him to whom the possession of the land belongs.
units.right_text: In the Year of Jubilee the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought — the original owner of the land.

units.left_text: All your valuations shall be according to the shekel of the sanctuary: twenty gerahs to the shekel.
units.right_text: Every valuation will be according to the sanctuary shekel, twenty gerahs to the shekel.

units.left_text: “‘However the firstborn among animals, which belongs to the LORD as a firstborn, no man may dedicate, whether an ox or a sheep. It is the LORD’s.
units.right_text: But no one may consecrate a firstborn of the livestock, because a firstborn belongs to the LORD. Whether it is an ox or a sheep, it is the LORD’s.

units.left_text: If it is an unclean animal, then he shall buy it back according to your valuation, and shall add to it the fifth part of it; or if it isn’t redeemed, then it shall be sold according to your valuation.
units.right_text: But if it is among the unclean animals, then he may redeem it according to your valuation and add a fifth of its value. If it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold according to your valuation.

units.left_text: “‘Notwithstanding, no devoted thing that a man devotes to the LORD of all that he has, whether of man or animal, or of the field of his possession, shall be sold or redeemed. Everything that is permanently devoted is most holy to the LORD.
units.right_text: Nothing that a man sets apart to the LORD from all he owns — whether a man, an animal, or his inherited land — can be sold or redeemed; everything so devoted is most holy to the LORD.

units.left_text: “‘No one devoted to destruction, who shall be devoted from among men, shall be ransomed. He shall surely be put to death.
units.right_text: No person set apart for destruction may be ransomed; he must surely be put to death.

units.left_text: “‘All the tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land or of the fruit of the trees, is the LORD’s. It is holy to the LORD.
units.right_text: Thus any tithe from the land, whether from the seed of the land or the fruit of the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.

units.left_text: If a man redeems anything of his tithe, he shall add a fifth part to it.
units.right_text: If a man wishes to redeem part of his tithe, he must add a fifth to its value.

units.left_text: All the tithe of the herds or the flocks, whatever passes under the rod, the tenth shall be holy to the LORD.
units.right_text: Every tenth animal from the herd or flock that passes under the shepherd’s rod will be holy to the LORD.

units.left_text: He shall not examine whether it is good or bad, neither shall he exchange it. If he exchanges it at all, then both it and that for which it is exchanged shall be holy. It shall not be redeemed.’”
units.right_text: He must not inspect whether it is good or bad, and he shall not make any substitution. But if he does make a substitution, both the animal and its substitute shall become holy; they cannot be redeemed.’”

units.left_text: These are the commandments which the LORD commanded Moses for the children of Israel on Mount Sinai.
units.right_text: These are the commandments that the LORD gave to Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
